lines.en: Tsubasa leads me away from the everblooming sakura into a hall full of old Japanese paintings I should probably know the names of but don’t.
I wouldn’t doubt if some of them are originals that I’m meant to be impressed by, but I refuse to be impressed by anything that’s so easily duplicated.
My untrained eye wanders from canvas to canvas, hoping to pick up even a fragment of what makes this dimension so palatable for someone like Tsubasa, but I get caught up on her instead.
Beauty is supposed to be in the eye of the beholder anyway. And despite how frequently these eyes deceive me, I know what it is that I would prefer to waste away my days observing.
There are no paintings that can bring me joy.
Maybe once upon a time there were-
But there aren’t any left now.
And if there are, I imagine they’re locked behind more doors in this palace than I’ll ever be able to open.
Tsubasa says some things as she leads me down the hall, but none of them attach to whatever part of my brain is meant to process them.
It isn’t until she leads me into a wide open, half-misty room that I remember what we’re doing or how to listen.
: This is one of Touka’s favorite additions to the manor and one that most people we bring here tend to enjoy very much.
: It’s nothing extravagant or historical like a special tree or a ceremonial room, but it houses a borderline-olympic sized heated pool.
: I used to spend a lot of time here when I was younger. I’m afraid I can seldom make the room in my schedule at this point, though.
: If there's anything I've learned today, it's that you’re a lot busier than I ever really imagined you were.
: Did you assume I was just some woman living off of her husband’s money without making an effort to actually accomplish anything?
: I don’t know if my thoughts were that specific.
: It’s that sort of perception that comes with the territory when you marry into the most influential family in a city.
: I can guarantee you I’ve heard it all before.
: Of course, though, that’s not even remotely true.
: I suppose it’s just in my nature to always be doing something. I have a hard time pulling myself away from anything that could be called “productive” in some form.
: Which is why you’ll see me...offering to give tours. Or offering to babysit. Or offering to check in on remote onsens for the sake of the family business.
: I suppose that last one was a tad relaxing, though.
: Even with all of the noise.
: I have no idea what you’re talking about. Chika and I were just watching TV.
: You’ll have to tell me what program. I can’t remember the last time I enjoyed watching TV that much.
: Wha-
: Sensei?
: What are you doing here?...
: Being shocked at how you’re still in [high_school].
: Yes, but what are you doing here?
: I invited him over to give him a tour of the manor, dear. I figured it was the least I could do to offer him thanks for his time at the arcade and...surrounding areas the other day.
: I see...
: Have you been in there this whole time?
: I’ve been in here for at least an hour. If I’d known you were coming, I would have put on something more presentable.
: No worries. What you’re wearing is totally fine.
: Are you enjoying the tour, at least? I’m assuming Mother already told you about the rock garden? She always likes to open up with that.
: I also showed him the golden room and told him all about how you’ve been dreaming of getting married there one day.
: Wha- Mother?!
: Sensei has no interest in that! And those were just silly, girlish dreams!
: Oh? So you don’t want to be married in the golden room anymore?
: I...well...
: Touka darling, come out of the pool if you’re going to hold a conversation with us. It’s bad manners staying in there.
: Hah...yes, Mother...
Touka exits the pool and wrings her hair back out into the water.
If her mother wasn’t standing beside me, I’d use this opportunity to make some perverted comment about the angle of her body as she does this.
But, at the risk of forming an erection in the process of mentally describing that, I will elect to abstain.
: Oh my. Are you still growing, dear? You may even surpass me at this rate.
Nevermind. Some things just can’t be contained.
: Mother, stop! Weren’t you just speaking of bad manners?!
: Oh, yes. Silly me. I was so impressed with your...progress, that I’d forgotten your teacher was even here.
: I completely understand. I forgot as well for a second.
: If you two are done objectifying me for now, I would like to go get dressed into something more suitable for the remainder of Sensei’s tour.
: Oh, his tour is just about over for the day. I’ve been dragging him around all morning. Though, I suppose he was willingly following me, so perhaps he enjoyed it?
: I just didn’t want to get lost in the entire mini-city you’ve built for yourselves.
: Have you really been here for that long? Why wasn’t I informed of this?
: I honestly didn’t even think you’d be okay with me coming.
: I’m...mostly indifferent to you coming. But if you’re here, I believe I should be involved in some way.
: I apologize for not telling you, dear. I’d just assumed you wanted the rest.
: My rest aside, I thought you had meetings today?
: I was on call for meetings regarding some of the properties we saw the other day- but it appears that none of them ever happened.
: Or at least no one’s been able to find me to inform me about them. You know our manor staff, though, so that doesn’t seem very probable.
: Well...regardless, I’m going to go get changed.
: Please inform me if you’re ever going to come here again. It’s one thing to appear casual at the dorms, but as the heiress of the Tsukioka Foundation, I can’t afford to be seen like this here.
: I have a reputation within the manor to uphold.
: I won’t tell anyone if you don’t, dear. Now, go get dressed. We’ll stay here until you return.
: Okay...
: Don’t go anywhere.
Touka grabs a towel off of a nearby rack and dries herself off before disappearing into the hall of a thousand paintings.
That’s not an accurate number- just an estimation.
: My lord. It feels like just the other day I was purchasing her luxury training bras.
: That’s an item that probably shouldn’t exist.
: But it does, and so she had them. Not for very long, though, as you can probably assume.
: So I guess we’re talking about your daughter’s breasts now. Not really how I imagined this tour ending after 90%% of it was a history lesson.
: Just some passing commentary. That wasn't a topic I intended to remain on any longer- at least not without her present for it.
: I feel like having her present for it would make things even weirder.
: Perhaps it would.
: Though, I wouldn’t say the same about what I feel we must discuss next.
: Which is?
: Would you find it rude if I took my shoes off? I don’t want to get in the pool, but I’d like to dip my feet in for a moment while we await my daughter’s return.
: Do whatever you want, it’s your house.
: Excellent. Then, don’t mind me.
Tsubasa sits down on a fancy looking beach chair and unstraps whatever the elegant looking sandal things she’s wearing are called.
She catches me looking at her for a moment and kindly waves me off so she can remove her stockings as well and, reluctantly, I oblige.
Once she’s done, she returns to me and sits down in front of the pool, hiking her dress up and dipping her toes into the water.
I sit beside her, mostly certain and even more uncomfortable about what I believe she wants to discuss next.
: Do you know what it is I want to talk about, Sensei?
: Probably, but I’d prefer to not guess and just have you get it over with so I don’t have to risk guessing incorrectly.
: Then I suppose I’ll “get it over with” and save us the difficulty of prodding at one another until it’s out in the open.
: A young lady who I’ve grown rather fond of lately seems to believe that the two of you are involved in an exclusive relationship with one another.
: But that young lady is just that. Young.
: And while I’m no stranger to the prospect of marrying someone older given that women have been traded between affluent families like cattle for centuries-
: I can’t help but get a little caught up when it comes to wrapping my mind around your situation.
You know, when I first told Tsubasa that I’d be okay with spending more time with her, I worried that something like this might come up.
She’s one of the only people Chika trusts enough to talk about our “relationship” with, which is kind of odd considering Tsubasa was, at one point, just some random woman at an onsen.
But she’s much more than that now. To Chika, at least.
And to Tsubasa, Chika is important as well.
So it only makes sense that she’d ask me about this now that she finally has an opportunity to.
The only issue is that I don’t know what the right thing or the wrong thing to say is.
Tsubasa seems like a rational and understanding person but, at the same time, she’s someone I’ve only known for a little while.
And I’m less important to her than a surrogate daughter.
In fact, I doubt I bear any sort of importance in Tsubasa’s life at all.
So, I should probably tread carefully here.
: What are you asking me?
: Oh? Is that a trace of attitude I’m hearing?
: Not intentionally. I’m just not sure how to answer a question that hasn’t been asked yet.
: And I’m not quite sure what I want to hear.
: On one hand, I want the young lady I care about to be happy. But when you really think about what it is that’s making her happy, the waters get a little muddy.
: I don’t-
: You are a grown man sleeping with a girl in [high_school]. Sleeping with your student.
: Aren’t you even a little worried about what could happen to you if that information were to get out?
: Are you grilling me as a friend or a parent right now?
: Can it not be both?
: Not when my answer would change based on yours.
: Then I suppose we can say I’m asking you as a friend.
: I see.
: Of course I’m worried about what would happen if that information were to get out.
: And yet, I don’t really do anything to try and stop it apart from just...asking her to keep quieter.
: Do you love her?
: Not the way I’m supposed to.
: And how is it you are supposed to love someone?
: The same way she loves me, I guess.
: Hm.
: You know, you can be pretty intimidating when you want to be.
: Women in power are good at that sort of thing.
: But if you want the truth, I’m not really appalled by what you do.
: Like I said, that sort of thing doesn’t mean much to me when I’ve gone my whole life hearing stories of other women from my family being shipped off to men twice their age.
: It loses its impact after a while.
: What I’m worried about is whether or not you’re going to hurt that young girl- whether it be intentional or unintentional. Because I don’t know if she’d be able to handle it.
: Just going to stay silent forever?
: Sometimes, silence is the best answer.
: And you think this is one of those times?
: I’m not sure what this is.
: But if I had to guess, I’d wager that I am going to hurt her.
: Life isn’t even half as convenient as it would need to be in order for me to avoid that.
: But I don’t intend to leave her side either.
: I don’t really think I could.
: Even if she winds up hating me for something I’ve done or...will do in the future, I’ll be there for her.
: So at least she won’t have to hurt alone.
: Granted, I’m not sure how much help my presence will be- especially when I’m worse at cheering people up or even just talking than anyone else I’ve ever met.
: But I’ll be there.
: She doesn’t have to be alone anymore.
I think about how the water would feel against my skin.
I shrug it off.
That’s all I ever do.
: That was a good answer.
: We can’t prevent ourselves from hurting the people we care about. All we can do is pray it doesn’t happen and be prepared to suture the wounds if it does.
: As long as you’re not just using the girl, I can accept the nature of your relationship.
: At first, that’s exactly what it was.
: But it’s not anymore, is it?
: Ah.
: Silence.
: It’s the best answer sometimes.
: I certainly picked an interesting class to enroll my daughter in, didn’t I?
: Probably the worst one possible. And I’ve always been a little curious about why.
: You’ve known about Chika and me since the beginning. I figured that would be all you need to know to keep Touka away.
: Tell me...How deep do you think this pool is, Sensei?
: What?
: When Touka was a little girl, she really wanted to learn how to swim.
: We hired an entire team of renowned instructors to teach her. People from all over the globe, since they were still allowed in back then.
: We spent so much money trying to help that little girl swim.
: But none of it worked.
: No matter who we hired or what their methods were, she just couldn’t learn.
: But one day, while the two of us were lounging near the poolside, I recalled a story one of my girlfriends told me about how she learned to swim when she was younger.
: Her mother pushed her into the pool.
: Terrified and wanting nothing more than to stay alive, her instincts kicked in and she managed to swim back to the ledge and pull herself out.
: You...pushed your daughter into the pool knowing full well she didn’t know how to swim?
: And now you’re her teacher.
: Sometimes, forcing people to do things they’re not comfortable with is the best way to move them forward.
: I’ve known from the beginning that you were the exact opposite of what Touka needs.
: And I think that’s exactly what makes her need you the most.
: Okay. But you have literally heard me have sex with a girl the same age as your daughter.
: Lots of it.
: Are we ending the conversation here?
: Yeah, I think we probably should.
Tsubasa and I sit in silence until Touka returns wearing the same white dress she had on when I first met her.
Everything goes back to normal.
And I, once again, manage to slip through the cracks of morality as I find that my newest acquaintance might also be a little broken as well.
Just in a much more beautiful way than I am.
Tsubasa’s affection has increased to [tsubasa_love]!
